---
number: 94
title: M2.5 Part 2: One semantics for every engine and exporter
milestone: M2.5
labels:
  - Epic
---

The SN P step is written four times (`NetworkSimulation`, the Metal kernel, the Verilog exporter, the Uppaal declarations), whether a rule applies six times, and the three delay kinds are inferred separately in five files, so every change to the model (synapse weights and an SMT encoding are next) has to be made everywhere and drifts.
We want the rule semantics in one place, a step API that every C# engine shares, and one compiled description of a network that every code generator reads, with engines, exporters and the hardware profile behind interfaces.

Its responsibilities are:
* Rule semantics: delay kind, applicability, what a rule produces, and the regex condition, each written once
* The step: release, deliver, the state key and output decoding split out of `NetworkSimulation`, and engines declaring what they support
* Generators (Verilog, Uppaal, Metal, NIR) reading one compiled description, behind an exporter interface with typed refusals
* The hardware profile as a value with typed problems, outside `Evolution`

`NetworkSimulation`'s release and deliver should be the source of truth, because every exporter is co-simulated against it.
Code generators will still emit the step in their own language, but the decisions (delay kind, produce, threshold table, closed or open) should be made once in the compiled description, because those decisions are what has drifted.

Order: rule semantics; step API and engines; compiled description and exporters; hardware profile.

Done when: delay kind, rule applicability and produce each have one definition that every engine and exporter uses, and the golden runs and co-simulation tests pass unchanged.

Read first: RESEARCH.md "Hardware profile and exporters", README "Engines", "Exporting to hardware"
